journey.name: File import — Anki .apkg and plain text, from picker to published deck
journey.description:
Bulk file import (#49, presentation layer finished in #55): pick a file, read a summary rather than a swipe queue, and publish. Covers the pieces that were built at one end only — rendered publish progress, the deck title the import already knows, the detected separator and its override — plus the failure modes that used to arrive as a parser message.
Requires a signed-in session (run journey 01 first) and two fixtures in the device's Downloads folder: an Anki `.apkg` export whose collection carries a real deck name, and a tab-separated "Notes in Plain Text" export. A third file that is not UTF-8 text (any photo) is needed for the wrong-file-type step.

actions.action: Launch the Loopky app and verify the Home screen is shown
Tap the element with resource-id "tab_decks"

Verify the file-import CTA (resource-id: decks_import_file) reads "Import from Anki or a file", is horizontally centred, and sits directly under the "Paste to import" card rather than separated from it by the section gap
Tap the element with resource-id "decks_import_file"

Verify the "Import file" screen opens on a real empty state — "Bring your deck over", a "WHAT WORKS" section with one card per accepted format (.apkg and .txt/.csv, each saying what it brings over and naming Anki's export path), a "Choose a file" button (resource-id: bulk_pick_file), and the size ceiling. It must NOT be a paragraph of prose over an otherwise blank screen
Verify the empty state ends with a "🤖 Let your AI build the deck" card — the landing page's prompt box — and that nothing offers to browse AnkiWeb
Verify six idea chips (resource-id: bulk_ai_idea_*), Anime selected, and the request field (resource-id: bulk_ai_request) holding the Naruto request
Tap "bulk_ai_idea_series" and verify the request field is replaced with the TV series request; type a few words into it and verify they stick

Tap the request field on a phone and verify the keyboard does not cover it, the page still scrolls to "See the full prompt" with the keyboard up, and there is no empty band between the content and the keyboard
Tap the element with resource-id "bulk_cli_copy" and verify its label flips to "Copied" for about two seconds, then back

Tap "bulk_ai_full_prompt" and verify the prompt (resource-id: bulk_ai_prompt_text) starts "Build me a Loopky flashcard deck with the Loopky CLI.", carries the edited request under "What I want:", and sends the agent to the Loopky plugin's skill with SKILL.md and the install.sh / install.ps1 fallbacks

Verify four "Open in" icons (resource-id: bulk_ai_open_claudecode / _codex / _jules / _cursor) with clear gaps between them, and that tapping Claude Code opens claude.ai/code?prompt= with that same prompt URL-encoded

On a tablet in portrait (medium width), verify one column with the full prompt already open and a "Using Claude Code or Codex?" block listing four plugin commands, EACH in its own row with its own copy button (resource-id: bulk_ai_copy_command) — never two commands in one copyable block, which Add Marketplace refuses as one bad owner/repo (loopky.github.io#19)
On a tablet in landscape (expanded width), verify the file import and the AI card stand side by side, and that scrolling the AI pane leaves the file pane where it is
Edit the request, rotate the tablet between portrait and landscape, and verify the edited request survives the change of layout
Tap the element with resource-id "bulk_pick_file" and choose the .apkg from Downloads
Verify a summary appears reading "N cards parsed" — NOT a swipe-triage queue, which nobody completes for a 20,000-card export
Verify the detected separator is shown (resource-id: bulk_separator_chip, e.g. "Separator: tab"). It was carried in state and rendered nowhere before #55
Verify a "Choose a different file" button (resource-id: bulk_repick) is present, so changing your mind is not a full restart
Tap the element with resource-id "bulk_separator_chip" and verify the override sheet opens listing separator options (resource-id: separator_option) — the same sheet the paste screen uses
Choose "comma" and verify the file re-parses: the card count drops to 0, a "N skipped (missing a front or back)" line appears, and the import button is disabled
Verify the skipped rows are genuinely dropped rather than merely reported — before #55 they reached publish and failed the whole import with "Card X has an empty side"
Tap "bulk_separator_chip" again, choose "tab", and verify the original card count returns
Tap the element with resource-id "bulk_import"
Verify the publish screen opens with the title field (resource-id: publish_title) PREFILLED with the .apkg's own deck name from its collection — not the file name, and not empty
Tap the element with resource-id "publish_button"

Verify a determinate progress bar (resource-id: publish_progress) and a live "Publishing N of M cards…" label (resource-id: publish_progress_label) appear, with N advancing — not an indeterminate spinner
Verify a "Cancel import" button (resource-id: publish_cancel) is shown alongside the bar
Verify the deck publishes and its detail screen shows the full card count
Return to Decks, tap "decks_import_file", and choose the tab-separated .txt export
Tap "bulk_import" and verify the title falls back to the file name with its extension stripped and underscores turned into spaces (e.g. "anki_export.txt" becomes "anki export")
Return to Decks, tap "decks_import_file", tap "bulk_pick_file" and choose a photo

Verify the error reads "That's not a text file" with advice to pick an .apkg or a plain-text export (resource-id: bulk_error) — NOT a parser message, and not a summary of junk cards decoded from the image bytes
Verify the error offers a retry that reopens the picker (resource-id: error_retry)
